#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Windows HostProcess containers mount files under a specified directory that is not recognized by client-go currently.  This means many components such as CNI's have to have workarounds to communicate with the api server.

More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/create-hostprocess-pod/#volume-mounts

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Plan to add a e2e test and currently testing with a CNI but wanted to get feedback

issue_context.title: Windows Hostprocess containers can't use the InClientConfig for api access
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

If you try to access the api service using Inclusterconfig  with Windows hostprocess container you get an error:

```
open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

#### What you expected to happen:

Should be able to connect to the API server. This is common scenario for kube-proxy and CNIs.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hostprocess-agnhost-older-client
spec:
  securityContext:
    windowsOptions:
      hostProcess: true
      runAsUserName: "NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM"
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: test
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    image: k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.32
    command:
      - powershell
      - -c
      - start-process
      - "-wait"
      - "-nonewwindow"
      - "$env:CONTAINER_SANDBOX_MOUNT_POINT\\agnhost"
    args:
      - "inclusterclient --poll-interval 5"
  restartPolicy: Always
  nodeSelector:
    "kubernetes.io/os": windows
  tolerations:
    - key: ""
      operator: "Exists"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
---
```

```
kubectl logs hostprocess-agnhost-older-client
I0825 00:12:40.693662    5192 main.go:61] started
I0825 00:12:40.758659    5192 log.go:184] err: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

review_comments: should this rely on the KEP-defined behavior and blindly prepend the envvar to the path? if it's empty, it'll no-op, and if it's populated, it is expected to hold a path that could be prepended in a manifest, right?

do the forward-slash-delimited paths above work as expected on windows, especially when combined with a backslash-delimited $CONTAINER_SANDBOX_MOUNT_POINT var?

per the example in the KEP, prepending would end up with paths looking like this:

`c:\c\<container id>\/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`

The win32 file APIs accept both (regardless of how strange it is...). I'd had a comment on sort of the same, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104490#discussion_r693276579. `filepath.Join` on a Windows host will actually correct it to the "windows" way of doing things, and adjust the unix like path to backslashes anyways. So 	`filepath.Join("C:\\path\\to\\thing", "/hello/world")` -> C:\\path\\to\\thing\\hello\\world, even if the first path ends with a trailing slash or no trailing slash.

@liggitt The logic here is basically: For Windows Server containers we don't want to change anything. The above will just get treated as an absolute path on the C drive which is what everyone's used to. If this env var is present, which is our tip off that this is a HostProcess container as 99% of the time I'd imagine that's the only time this would be present, then we want to join the path with where the rootfs for the container is on the host.
if simple concatenation work, I think we should limit ourselves to that, since that is what use of the envvar in args, commands, and workingDir is limited to
Sure, that sounds reasonable to me

We joined here as in the other spots we're taking user input and simply expanding to what the envvar contains. Here, there is none and we're just taking what the previous logic was and having it point to the new location, seemed better to have a more friendly looking path even if the gnarly looking one will work for the file apis.
inClusterClientConfig#Namespace() and inClusterClientConfig#Possible() also reference this path
